comparisons.peer_topic: Noninterest expense increase drivers and prior year comparisons
comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense increased $967 million to $66.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses and investments in people, operations, and technology, partially offset by higher FDIC expense in 2023 (including a $2.1 billion special assessment) and lower expenses from a liquidating business activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the composition of noninterest/operating expenses and the impact of FDIC assessments. Citigroup noted that higher legal and volume-related expenses were offset by productivity savings, resulting in largely unchanged total expenses. In contrast, Bank of America reported a $967 million increase in noninterest expense, noting that higher FDIC expenses in the prior year (including a $2.1 billion special assessment) were partially offset by current year investments in people and technology. While Citi's net result was flat, BAC's was up, but both cite FDIC special assessment history as a key comparability factor in their expense trends.

sentences.text: Expenses were largely unchanged, as higher legal expenses and higher volume-related expenses were offset by productivity savings.
Noninterest expense increased $967 million to $66.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023.

The increase was primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology, partially offset by higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023, including $2.1 billion for the estimated special assessment amount arising from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.

comparisons.peer_topic: Factors driving 2024 operating expense decreases and increases
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses decreased relative to 2023 due to lower commercial real estate impairments, GreenSky intangible asset write-downs, consumer platform goodwill impairments, and FDIC fees, partially offset by higher compensation and transaction-based expenses driven by improved performance. An additional $71 million FDIC special assessment fee was recognized in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs reported year-over-year decreases in total operating expenses in 2024, primarily driven by the absence of significant prior-year one-time charges or impairments, specifically FDIC special assessment fees and commercial real estate impairments. While Citi's expenses were 'largely unchanged' due to offsetting higher legal/volume expenses with productivity savings, Goldman Sachs saw a 2% decrease explicitly attributed to lower CIE commercial real estate impairments and the FDIC special assessment fee, partially offset by higher compensation.

sentences.text: Expenses were largely unchanged, as higher legal expenses and higher volume-related expenses were offset by productivity savings.

Operating expenses, compared with 2023, reflected decreases driven by significantly lower expenses, including impairments ($1.46 billion recognized in 2023), related to commercial real estate in CIEs (largely in depreciation and amortization) and other significant expenses recognized in the prior year, including the write-down of identifiable intangible assets related to GreenSky of $506 million and an impairment of goodwill related to Consumer platforms of $504 million (both in depreciation and amortization), and the FDIC special assessment fee of $529 million (in other expenses).
These decreases were partially offset by higher compensation and benefits expenses (reflecting improved operating performance) and higher transaction based expenses.

An incremental expense for the FDIC special assessment fee of $71 million was recognized in 2024, as the FDIC notified banks subject to the special assessment fee of the updated estimated cost to the Deposit Insurance Fund resulting from the closures in 2023 of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.
